title: Perfect complexes have a set of representatives
statement: For every quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X [def-pc-scheme], the full subcategory of perfect complexes [def-pc-perfect-complex] in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] has a set of representatives up to isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh, set-of-representatives input for perfect complexes

proof.text: Let W = Spec(A) be an affine open. By [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] (Stacks 08EB), every perfect object of D_QCoh(O_W) is isomorphic to the complex of quasi-coherent sheaves associated with a bounded complex P^\bullet of finite projective A-modules. Each finite projective A-module is isomorphic to a direct summand of some A^n, hence to a submodule of some A^n, and these submodules form a set; so every such P^\bullet is isomorphic, as a complex, to one whose terms are submodules of finite free modules A^n and whose differentials are A-linear maps between them, and these data (a finite range of degrees, terms, and differentials) form a set. Isomorphic complexes give isomorphic objects of the derived category, so the isomorphism classes of perfect objects on W form a set.

source.place: Theorem perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh, set-of-representatives input for perfect complexes

proof.text: Let P(W) assert that perfect objects of D_QCoh(O_W) have a set of isomorphism representatives. Suppose W = U union V with U quasi-compact and V affine open, and P(U), P(V), and P(U intersect V). For E perfect on W, each restriction of E to an open is again perfect (restrict the covering in [def-pc-perfect-complex]), and U, V, U intersect V are quasi-compact opens of the qcqs scheme W, so the derived Mayer–Vietoris triangle [lem-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-triangle] expresses E as the first object of a distinguished triangle whose other terms are R(j_U)_*E|_U direct-sum R(j_V)_*E|_V and R(j_{U intersect V})_*E|_{U intersect V}. Choose representatives for the three restrictions using P(U), P(V), and P(U intersect V); transporting along the chosen isomorphisms, the second morphism of the triangle becomes a morphism between the derived direct images of the three representatives. For fixed representatives, the Hom-set between these two objects of the derived category is a set, so the possible morphisms form a set, and E is isomorphic to a cocone of one of them; each cone (equivalently, cocone) is unique up to isomorphism once this morphism is fixed, by the triangulated-category morphism-of-triangles axiom (TR3) and the five-lemma. Thus P(W) holds. The qcqs induction principle [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] then gives P(X) from the affine case of Step 1 and this gluing implication.
